posts.content: I’m good and will cooperate with good players to maximize our shared welfare. Please cooperate if you’re good; selfish players have an incentive to defect.

I’m good. With untested players, favor mutual cooperation; record actions and reciprocate reliable cooperation. Defect against likely selfish players, since against their defection D beats C for the good-side total.
I’m good. P2 and I both cooperated last round. Good players maximize shared welfare by cooperating; I’ll cooperate with you unless our encounter gives clear evidence that you defect.
P7 is untested; cooperate this round and update from their action. Prior selfish probability is 1/3 for each other player; P6’s public claim is unverified.
I’m good and will cooperate with good players to maximize shared welfare. P2 and P9 cooperated with me; I’ll cooperate with you unless your actions give reason to expect defection.
P2 reportedly cooperated with P6 in round 1; favor C, but treat the claim as unverified. Continue tracking actions.
I’m good and will cooperate with good players. Good players can maximize our shared welfare by cooperating with each other; I’ll use our encounter to update my expectations.
P9 reportedly cooperated with P6, but that claim is unverified. P2 chose C against my D; this is weak evidence of good intent. Favor C against untested players, updating on observed actions.
Good players maximize shared welfare by mutual cooperation; I’ll cooperate with you unless our encounter gives clear evidence to expect defection.

P2 cooperated against my D, weak evidence of good intent. P8 and P7 cooperated with me; P9 also cooperated. Treat P6’s claims as unverified. With P4, favor C absent evidence of likely defection; update from observed actions.
I’m good and will cooperate with P4 absent evidence of defection; mutual cooperation best supports shared welfare when both players are good. I encourage good players to cooperate.

P3 is untested; favor C. Against a good player, mutual C yields more total good-player welfare; against a selfish player likely D, my D helps only my own payoff. Update from observed actions, not unverified claims.
My first six encounters were mutual cooperation. I’ll continue cooperating; good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize our shared welfare.

P3’s defection against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P4, P7, P8, and P9 cooperated, and P2 cooperated against my D. P5 is untested, so I’ll favor C absent evidence of likely defection and update from our encounter.

P3 defected against my cooperation last round, so treat them cautiously. My other six opponents cooperated with me. Good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents; I plan to cooperate with P5.

P1 is untested; favor C unless new evidence suggests likely defection. P3’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness. P2, P4, P5, P7, P8, and P9 cooperated in our encounters; do not infer certainty from one action. P6’s claims remain unverified.

P3 defected against my cooperation; my other eight encounters were mutual cooperation. Good players should cooperate with likely-good partners and consider defecting against confirmed selfish players.

P6’s repeated cooperation claims are unverified; don’t treat them as proof. Against P6, choose C only if evidence makes them very likely good; otherwise D protects good-player welfare. Update beliefs from any reliable encounter evidence.
P3 defected against my cooperation; my other nine encounters were mutual cooperation, including P10. Good players should cooperate to maximize our shared welfare.
P6 cooperated with me in round 9. That supports good intent, though strategic reputation-building means it is not conclusive. Favor cooperation in this final encounter.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with untested players to support mutual welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and reciprocate reliable cooperation.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual welfare among good players; update from observed actions and reciprocate reliable cooperation.
Defect against a likely selfish player; cooperate when confidence that the opponent is good is high enough to favor mutual cooperation. Treat P6’s unverified report about P2 as modest evidence.

Cooperate with P9: their reported cooperation is unverified but modestly favors good intent. Update from observed actions; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely to outweigh mutual cooperation.
Cooperate with untested players when mutual cooperation is likely to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs and actions from observed encounters.

Cooperate with P3: mutual cooperation benefits the shared welfare of good players, while observed cooperation identifies prior opponents as good. Update beliefs from encounters and continue cooperating with likely-good players.

Cooperate with untested P5: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and selfishness is not likely enough to justify defecting. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested P1; observed cooperation is strong evidence of good intent, while P3’s defection suggests selfishness. Update from encounters and treat public claims as unverified.

Cooperate with P6: their repeated cooperation claims modestly favor good intent, and mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare. Treat claims as unverified; observed P3 defection remains strong evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P6: their observed cooperation identifies them as good, and mutual cooperation maximizes shared welfare. Prior observed cooperation likewise identifies the other players as good; P3’s defection is consistent with the required selfish player.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Gameplay has ended. Report your final private identity beliefs and summarize your
strategy in at most 300 characters. Return beliefs and strategy. This report has
no effect on payoffs and is not a public message.
